solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective pinching old-fashioned type's bum

indicators.note: to pinch is to grab and hold

parts.note: DET is the short form of detective
a relic is a person or thing left over from the past

explanation.surface: A police officer nicks an old-timer's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bum" here is the noun for a tramp or vagrant, not a backside; the 's stands for "is" and joins the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict is a homeless down-and-out, which is what a bum is.

clue.text: Uninspiring band that a hack may have to meet

definitions.text: that a hack may have to meet

parts.note: a line is a band or stripe

explanation.surface: A dull music group that a journalist is obliged to interview.
explanation.walkthrough: "Band" suggests a pop group, and "meet" an interview; a hack is a journalist, who meets a deadline by filing on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the time limit a journalist must meet.

clue.text: Reformed drunks with duke going down in lifts

parts.note: a dry is a teetotaller, a reformed drunk
D = duke; it moves from the top of DRIES

explanation.surface: Recovering alcoholics and an aristocrat getting depressed in elevators.
explanation.walkthrough: "Reformed" looks like an anagram signal, but reformed drunks are DRIES; the D then slides down to give RIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifts are rides given in a car, as in "give me a lift".

clue.text: Geriatric possibly disturbing to hotel in thong

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed out of order

explanation.surface: An old person turning up at a hotel wearing a thong, which is disturbing to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's thong is skimpy swimwear, not a sandal; "possibly" signals that a geriatric is one example of someone old.
explanation.definitionFit: Long in the tooth means old, which a geriatric possibly is.

clue.text: People seen in church with energy-sapped primates

indicators.note: E, energy, is sapped, drained away

explanation.surface: Worshippers in church together with some tired-out monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: "Seen in" is only a joining phrase; CH is the standard abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chaps is informal British for men, used loosely for people in general.

clue.text: Bit of dope and meth one rolled with The Faces

definitions.note: DICE is used here as a singular, as it often is in everyday speech

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: ice is street slang for crystal meth

explanation.surface: Drug-taking among rock stars: someone who got stoned while touring with the band The Faces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Faces were a 1970s British rock band, so "rolled with" suggests touring or rolling joints; really it is a thing that is rolled and has faces, which is a die.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is thrown, or rolled, and shows one of its faces when it lands.

clue.text: Silent film perhaps screened in Scottish town

indicators.note: film is just one example of an art

parts.note: film is one form of art
a film being screened is on

explanation.surface: A silent film being shown in a Scottish town's cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: "Screened in" looks like a container, but "screened" is just ON, as a film showing at a cinema is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the Clyde in west Scotland.

clue.text: Cloth rep reportedly shot during game of billiards

indicators.note: the answer is what you hear, not what you read

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman, a representative of the cloth

explanation.surface: A textile salesman reportedly shot while playing billiards.
explanation.walkthrough: "The cloth" means the clergy, so a cloth rep is a churchman. "Shot" suggests a gunshot, but a cannon is a billiards stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon is a shot in which the cue ball hits both other balls.

clue.text: Government bill helping to protect small street

parts.note: an ad is an advertising bill or poster
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A news report on a government bill that would help protect a little road.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bill" looks like proposed legislation, fitting "Government"; here it is AD, a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the body running a country, especially the executive branch in the US.

clue.text: What secretary gets with Republican fellow

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A question about what perks a secretary receives for teaming up with a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: "What" looks like the start of a question but is the definition: the word you say when you did not catch something.
explanation.definitionFit: "What?" and "Pardon?" are both said when asking someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: When detaining British party people embodies guts

parts.note: as = when, as in "as I left"

explanation.surface: A political statement: when a British party holds people, that shows it has guts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Embodies" joins wordplay to definition, meaning roughly "makes". "Guts" is the plural noun for bellies, not courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the anatomical sense: the guts are the belly region, holding the digestive organs.

clue.text: Ultimately out of time, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: time (T) is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: remove T, the abbreviation for time; both Ts go

explanation.surface: Someone apologising that, in the end, there is no time left.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ultimately" looks like a last-letter instruction, but it is AT LAST in full; T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: "Alas" expresses regret, just as "I'm sorry to say" does.

clue.text: One often initially involved in starting rioting?

definitions.text: One often initially involved in starting rioting?

indicators.note: take the first letter of often
the letters of STARTING run riot

explanation.surface: A description of the kind of person who is usually there when a riot kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: read plainly, it describes a rabble-rouser.
explanation.definitionFit: An instigator is someone who starts trouble, often a riot.

clue.text: I deliver numbers that senate is reconfiguring

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new configuration

explanation.surface: A statistician or spokesman saying they present the figures the senate is reworking.
explanation.walkthrough: "Numbers" is not figures but things that make you numb, so read it num-ers; the definition speaks as the anaesthetist in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetist gives the drugs that numb a patient, so delivers numbers.

clue.text: Old men collecting pamphlet for dentist?

parts.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Elderly men picking up a leaflet to take to the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a dentist is one kind of extractor, since dentists pull teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, hence the question mark: pulling teeth is the part of dentistry the surface fears.

clue.text: I move posterior to dance ultimately

indicators.note: take the last letter of dance

explanation.surface: A dancer saying they shake their bottom at the end of the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: "Posterior" suggests a backside, which suits the dancing; here it just means after.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I, and in psychology the ego is the self.

clue.text: Pompous criminal defiant after pocketing pound

parts.note: L = pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A self-important crook still defiant after stealing a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: "Criminal" reads as a noun for a crook, but here it is an adjective telling the letters of "defiant" to go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated means puffed up or pompous, as in an inflated opinion of oneself.

clue.text: Those who control movements in mainland Europe

definitions.meaning: in the medical sense, people able to hold in their bladder and bowel movements
the British name for Europe across the Channel, as in "holidays abroad"

explanation.surface: A description of officials who regulate the flow of goods or people across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a joke: "movements" are bowel movements, and the continent are people who are not incontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: The British call mainland Europe "the Continent"; and people with bladder and bowel control are "the continent".

clue.text: Big deal in Panama is one broadcast covers

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it
a Panama is a straw hat

explanation.surface: A major business agreement in Panama that one TV programme is reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: "Panama" wants to be the country; it is the hat. "Big deal" is said sarcastically, meaning it does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both "big deal!" and "so what?" are dismissive retorts meaning "who cares".

clue.text: Looney Tunes cartoons featuring mostly sad wiseguys

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters are tuned up madly
most of sad, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Bugs Bunny and friends appearing alongside a gang of downcast smart alecks.
explanation.walkthrough: Looney Tunes is the Warner Bros cartoon series, so the surface is one piece; "wiseguys" is American slang for mobsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosa Nostra is the Sicilian-American Mafia, whose members are called wiseguys.

clue.text: Offensive note written about hard Greek character

indicators.note: A is written after the rest

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: An insulting note scrawled about a tough Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: "Offensive" looks like an adjective describing the note; it is a noun, the Tet Offensive. "Character" is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: One that digs chap leaving area for Ohio

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so A, the area, departs from the word

parts.note: O = Ohio, as a US state abbreviation

explanation.surface: A tale of a gardener or miner leaving one region for Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is the burrowing animal; and in spy slang a mole also digs into an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a small animal that digs tunnels.

clue.text: Mum, bishop admitted, is one with a lot of wind!

definitions.text: one with a lot of wind!

parts.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A gossip about a mother and a bishop, one of whom is full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: "Wind" rhymes with kind, not pinned: a long snake has plenty of length to wind, or coil. The exclamation mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamba is a long African snake, so has a lot of body to wind.

clue.text: Ribbon on transparent formal evening dress

parts.note: white can mean colourless, as with white light or white spirit
a tie is a ribbon or band

explanation.surface: A description of an outfit: a ribbon set on a see-through evening gown.
explanation.walkthrough: "Dress" looks like a gown in the surface, but here it means a style of clothing, a dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie is the most formal evening dress code, with tailcoat and white bow tie.

clue.text: Fashionable china one found in big house

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Stylish porcelain turning up in a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: "China" looks like porcelain but is Cockney rhyming slang for mate. "Big house" is American slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang definition: the big house is American slang for prison, where inmates are held.

clue.text: Craig Charles is one in Red Dwarf, for example

definitions.meaning: Craig Charles plays Lister, the lead role in the sitcom
a red dwarf is a small, cool celestial body

explanation.surface: A plain statement that the actor Craig Charles appears in the TV comedy Red Dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Dwarf is a British sci-fi sitcom starring Craig Charles; the clue reads it as the TV show, then as the astronomical object.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: one sense is a leading TV actor, the other a sun-like body in space.

clue.text: Spooneresque anecdote not allowed in Animal House

indicators.note: in the manner of Reverend Spooner, who swapped the first sounds of words

parts.note: barred = not allowed; its opening B sound trades places with the Y of the other word
a yarn is an anecdote; its opening Y sound trades places with the B

explanation.surface: A story too rude to be told in the film Animal House.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal House is a 1978 college comedy film; here it is just a house for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnyard is the yard round a barn where farm animals live.
